subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should this timestamped-backup PR preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups are recovery and sensitive-data artifacts, so changing shipped retention and chmod behavior is an upgrade decision that should be explicit before merge.

options.title: Require Upgrade-Safe Migration
options.body: Keep this PR open but require preserving or converting legacy `.bak.N` files until retention is safely replenished, with proof for fresh and upgrade paths.

options.title: Accept First-Write Cleanup
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept deletion of legacy numeric backups, but the PR should document that upgrade behavior and prove the remaining recovery path is acceptable.

options.title: Pause For Broader Backup Layout
options.body: Pause or close this PR if the dedicated backup-directory request should own both naming and storage layout.

recommendation.title: Require Upgrade-Safe Migration
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but require preserving or converting legacy `.bak.N` files until retention is safely replenished, with proof for fresh and upgrade paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history around config backup and recovery semantics for this upgrade-behavior choice.
